data.name: Haajib
data.gender_notes: Haajib is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root h-j-b, which means ‘to cover,’ ‘to attend,’ or ‘to serve.’ This name is often given to those who serve important figures or serve in a religious capacity. The name Haajib carries the meaning “Servant, attendant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Haajib usually hope their child will grow to embody servant, attendant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: To serve Allah and His Prophet with utmost devotion and humility.
data.etymology: Haajib belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant, attendant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haajib total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: حاجب
in_arabic.meaning: حاجب تعني الشخص الذي يمنع أو يحجب الشيء
in_arabic.long_meaning: حاجب هو اسم مشتق من الجذر العربي 'حجب' والذي يعني ستر أو تغطية الشيء. في اللغة العربية، الحاجب هو الشخص الذي يحجب أو يمنع الشيء عن الآخرين. وقد ورد هذا الاسم في القرآن الكريم في سياق الحديث عن الأئمة والمرشدين الروحيين الذين يحجبون أو يمنعون الناس عن الضلال. وفي التاريخ الإسلامي، كان الحاجب هو الشخص الذي يتولى حماية وحراسة المسجد الحرام في مكة المكرمة.

in_urdu.name: حاجب
in_urdu.meaning: حاجب مطلب ہے جو چیز کو چھپاتا یا روکتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: حاجب عربی جڑ 'حجب' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے ستر یا ڈھانپنا۔ اردو میں، حاجب کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو کسی چیز کو چھپاتا یا روکتا ہے۔ اسلامی تقالید میں، حاجب کا استعمال ان شخصیات کے لئے کیا جاتا ہے جو روحانی رہبری प्रदान کرتے ہیں اور لوگوں کو گمراہی سے بچاتے ہیں۔ جنوبی ایشیا میں مسلم کمیونٹی میں، یہ نام روایتی اور تاریخی اہمیت رکھتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हाजिब
in_hindi.meaning: हाजिब का अर्थ है जो व्यक्ति किसी चीज़ को छुपाता या रोकता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: हाजिब नाम अरबी जड़ 'حجب' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है ढकना या छुपाना। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, हाजिब नाम का अर्थ है वह व्यक्ति जो किसी चीज़ को छुपाता या रोकता है। यह नाम उन आध्यात्मिक नेताओं के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो लोगों को सही रास्ते पर ले जाते हैं और उन्हें गुमराह होने से बचाते हैं।

in_pashto.name: حاجب
in_pashto.meaning: حاجب دى هغه کسانو معنی چې کوم څه پټوي يا مخه يې نيسي
in_pashto.long_meaning: حاجب په عربي ژبه کې د 'حجب' له ريښې څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې معنی يې ده پټول يا پوښول. په پښتنو او افغانانو کې، حاجب هغه څوک دی چې کوم څه پټوي يا مخه يې نيسي. دا نوم د هغو روحاني مشرانو لپاره کارول کېږي چې خلکو ته لارښوونه کوي او د ګمراهۍ څخه يې بچوي.

in_english.name: Haajib
in_english.meaning: Haajib means the one who prevents or covers something
in_english.long_meaning: The name Haajib is derived from the Arabic root 'ḥ-j-b' which means to cover or prevent. In Islamic tradition, Haajib refers to a person who provides spiritual guidance and prevents others from going astray. The name has historical significance in Islamic culture, particularly in reference to leaders and guardians of sacred spaces.

data.cultural_impact: In the Islamic context, the term "Haajib" is used to refer to a person, usually a eunuch, who serves a royal court or a high-ranking individual, often as a personal attendant. Historically, eunuchs served many roles in Islamic societies, ranging from military leaders and administrators to roles as teachers, doctors, musicians, and poets. In Arabic and Middle Eastern cultures, eunuchs were often highly respected and influential figures.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Haajib" holds spiritual significance as it is derived from the Arabic root h-j-b, which also means 'to cover.' In Islamic tradition, covering oneself is seen as an important aspect of modesty and respect, particularly for women. The name Haajib, therefore, can be seen as a reminder of the importance of modesty and respect in one's religious practice. Additionally, the root h-j-b is also used in the term "hajj," which refers to the Islamic pilgrimage to Mecca. Thus, the name can also be seen as a reminder of the spiritual journey that every Muslim is called to undertake in their lifetime.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'The Muqaddimah'. In this seminal work on history and sociology, the 14th-century Islamic scholar describes the Haajib as a military official and aide to the sultan, who would lead the sultan's personal guard during military campaigns.
historical_references.context: Military role in the sultan's court

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi's 'The History of the Administration of Egypt'. This 15th-century historian recounts how the Haajib served as a chief financial administrator and advisor to the Mamluk sultans of Egypt, managing the state's revenues and maintaining the sultan's palace.
